metadata.title: Paramedical and Mental Health Practice Platform Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: Explore how a Dutch healthcare software group of about 250 people in the Netherlands and Switzerland, serving 40,000+ healthcare professionals and 4 million+ patients with practice management and EPD labels for paramedical care (HCI One, FysioRoadmap, SpotOnMedics, Incura, Evry, ParaNICE), the CRS EPD for mental health care, the Uw Zorg Online and Quli patient environments and the Embloom e-health platform, certified for NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 and backed by Vortex Capital Partners in a buy-and-build since 2021, would need to change when Vecozo and the GDS801 declaration standard change and rejections spike, the NZa rewrites the zorgprestatiemodel with a mandatory referral date, ransomware or a cloud outage hits the multi-tenant EPD, MedMij and Wegiz make PGO disclosure mandatory for paramedical care, the migration of a label into HCI One stalls and practices churn to Intramed, insurers move to outcome-based contracts that need PROMs and LDF data, an AI voice-to-text error ends up in a clinical note and a complaint, a GP information system vendor launches its own patient app and drops the Uw Zorg Online connection, consolidation among GGZ institutions locks CRS out of the top 50, or labour shortage and the 'ontregel de zorg' programme change what practices are willing to pay for.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: A practice signs with one label, its therapists get accounts, and the agenda becomes the heart of the practice: patients book online or by phone, treatments are recorded in the dossier with the discipline's care pathway and templates, measurements and PROMs are entered during the trajectory, and every registered treatment produces a declaration line that goes to the insurer through Vecozo overnight while patient invoices go out with a Mollie link. Return messages are corrected by the practice or by HCI's billing service, monthly pseudonymised data goes to the LDF and the Keurmerk register, dashboards summarise production and revenue, and the practice website links to online booking. GGZ organisations run CRS with treatment plans, medication, ROM through Embloom and declarations under the zorgprestatiemodel or contracts with municipalities. Patients use Uw Zorg Online to reach their GP, pharmacy or therapist and Quli to collect their data from several providers under MedMij. HCI's own consultants onboard practices, migrate acquired labels into HCI One and answer support tickets. The design assumes that a declaration standard changes once a year with a long notice period, that a zorgprestatiemodel rule is a validation in the declaration screen, that one multi-tenant EPD environment is one blast radius and that a backup is a recovery plan, that PGO disclosure is a Quli feature rather than an obligation on every EPD, that a migration is a project with a date, that an insurer pays per treatment and quality is a monthly export, that a transcribed note is the therapist's text, that a GP information system connector is a stable channel to a patient, that a GGZ institution keeps its EPD for a decade, and that practices pay per user for a system whose value is the administration it holds.
metadata.residualArchitecture: The changed design separates declaration standard and version with effective period, message schema and validation rule set, submission batch and return-message reason code, rejection pattern and correction playbook, financing rule set version with effective date, referral record with date and source, registration completeness check and pre-submission gate, tenant, cell and blast radius, immutable backup and restore drill, incident and affected-tenant set, degraded mode and read-only dossier, disclosure obligation per care sector and information standard version, PGO disclosure endpoint and consent per EPD, label, migration wave, parity gap and rollback plan, practice sentiment and churn risk signal, contract type, outcome measure and payer data product, PROM completion and consent per trajectory, AI capability, model version and provider, transcript provenance, human edit record and clinical sign-off, patient channel, connector and channel fallback, practice-facing patient relationship independent of a HIS, institution segment, tender package and portal parity, exit and data-portability path, administrative-burden metric per practice, automation entitlement and value-based packaging. A declaration knows which standard version, rule set, referral and correction produced it; a dossier survives a tenant incident; a patient relationship survives a dropped connector; a label can move into HCI One in waves with a way back; and a practice can change label, contract type, AI policy or package without changing systems.
metadata.note: The stressors start in the Dutch first-line and mental health care trade: the GDS801 declaration standard that replaced PM304 on 1 January 2025 and the Vecozo gateway, the NZa zorgprestatiemodel with its 2026 mandatory referral date, NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 and the WGBO 20-year retention, Wegiz in force since April 2023 and the MedMij afsprakenstelsel with 16 labelled PGOs in November 2025, Intramed's calculated 53 percent share of physiotherapy practices in the 2017 Marktdata survey, insurers' quality contracting on LDF and Keurmerk data, the EU AI Act and WGBO liability for clinical documentation, the HIS/AIS vendors Pharmapartners, CGM, Sanday and HealthConnected, the M&I/Partners 2025 inventory in which SDB Groep and Nedap serve 15 and 14 of the 50 largest GGZ organisations (30 and 27 percent), the VFW finding that physiotherapists lose a working day per week to administration, and the Vortex thesis of integrating labels into HCI One while expanding digital patient access. They are not forecasts and assign no likelihood; each asks what must remain after the company is pushed into a different attractor. The declaration-standard, financing-rule and security scenarios are recorded as residues the platform already carries; the labour-shortage and administrative-burden shift is the loop that tests whether those residues hold without new structure.

source.title: Residues: Time, Change, and Uncertainty in Software Architecture
source.author: Barry M. O'Reilly

stressors.name: Vecozo and the GDS801 declaration standard change again and rejections spike across 40,000 professionals
stressors.detection: Vektis publications of a new GDS801 version or an intermediate release of the paramedical declaration standard, Vecozo notices about gateway certificate, endpoint or message-envelope changes, ZN and insurer-specific validation rules announced through PPN and KNGF, the share of submitted declaration lines returned with a rejection code per insurer per week, return messages whose reason code is unknown to the correction playbook, billing-service backlog of return messages older than five days, support tickets that mention 'afgekeurd' or 'retourbericht', cash-flow complaints from practice owners whose payment run slipped, insurer helpdesk waiting times, comparison threads in which practices ask whether Intramed had the same rejections, and the number of labels that need the same fix applied separately.
stressors.attractor: A GDS801 revision with a new mandatory field and tightened validation lands with three months' notice, one large insurer applies it early and another late, and Vecozo rotates its gateway certificates in the same quarter. In the naive design each label has its own declaration module, the standard is compiled into the export, a rejection is a text in a return message that a practice or the billing service reads by hand, a correction is a re-submission of the whole batch, and the same fix is built five times. Within two weeks the first-time acceptance rate for the affected insurer drops from 97 to 80 percent, 200,000 declaration lines wait in correction, practices on the label that fixed it last read on forums that HCI is 'the vendor whose declarations bounce', the billing service hires temps, and the declaration volume that flows through HCI (more than EUR 500 million a year already in 2022) becomes the reason practice owners consider switching rather than the reason they stay.
stressors.businessReaction: Model the declaration standard as a versioned message schema with an effective period, per-insurer rule sets and a validation gate that runs before submission across every label; treat a return message as a structured reason code mapped to a correction playbook that the practice, the billing service or an automated re-submission can execute line by line; separate the Vecozo gateway (certificates, endpoints, envelopes) from the declaration content so a gateway change never touches a rule; run every standard change as one release for all labels with a dry-run against last month's declarations; expose a rejection dashboard per insurer and per reason to practices and to HCI; and publish the rejection rate and correction lead time as a service level that the billing service and the platform share.
stressors.residue: Separate declaration standard and version with effective period, per-insurer validation rule set, pre-submission validation gate, gateway configuration, submission batch and line, return-message reason code, correction playbook and re-submission, rejection pattern per insurer, label-independent declaration release, and rejection dashboard. A declaration knows which standard version and rule set validated it and which correction resolved it, whatever label produced it.

impacts.effect: Practice owners keep 'every treatment declared and paid without rework' through a standard change because the change is a rule release, not a scramble per label.
GGZ practitioners see the same validation gate protect zorgprestatiemodel claims that protects paramedical GDS801 declarations.
Consultants and the billing service work rejection queues by reason code and playbook instead of reading return messages one by one.
Declarations are validated against the version in force before they leave the practice, so a standard change shows up as warnings, not as rejections.
Discipline-specific declaration rules (speech therapy, dietetics, podiatry) live in the same versioned rule set and change on the same release.
Institutions see per-financier rule sets and rejection patterns for insurers and municipalities side by side.
Return-message issues resolve through a playbook per reason code with a lead-time target instead of ad-hoc expertise.
Accounting and payment partners receive declaration status changes as versioned events rather than as re-exported batches.
Administration minutes per treatment do not spike when a standard changes because corrections are line-level and largely automated.
Direct client time share is protected because rejection handling does not fall back on the practitioner.
Ships one declaration engine for all disciplines with versioned standards and a pre-submission gate.
Consumes the shared declaration release instead of its own compiled export.
Consumes the shared declaration release and exposes the rejection dashboard next to its BI.
Runs the billing service on reason codes, playbooks and a shared correction lead-time target.
Adds the validation gate, structured return messages and line-level correction to the flow from registration to payment.
Reports rejection rate and correction lead time per insurer and reason.
Publishes declaration status as versioned events to accounting and payment partners.
Holds standard versions with effective periods, per-insurer rule sets and the pre-submission validation gate.
Isolates gateway certificates, endpoints and envelopes from declaration content and parses return messages into reason codes.

stressors.name: The NZa rewrites zorgprestatiemodel rules mid-cycle and every GGZ declaration needs a referral date and new professional codes
stressors.detection: NZa beleidsregels and nadere regels for the zorgprestatiemodel published in the summer for the next year, Vektis release notes for the GGZ declaration standard, the 2026 rule that every declaration carries a referral date and the end of the transitional benefit, additions to the professional standards such as the system therapist, insurer contract addenda that reference the new fields, the share of open trajectories in CRS without a referral record, declarations returned for a missing or invalid referral date, GGZ institutions asking how to backfill referrals for clients who entered in 2023, municipal iJw and iWmo version changes in the same window, waiting-time reporting that changes definition, support tickets from practice owners who discover in January that December's registrations cannot be claimed, and consultants configuring the same setting in dozens of tenants.
stressors.attractor: From 1 January every zorgprestatiemodel declaration must carry a referral date and source, a new professional category is added, indexation changes tariffs for independent practitioners, and the NZa clarifies a setting rule in March with retroactive effect to January. In the naive design a referral is a free-text field in the intake, the rule is a validation in the declaration screen, tariffs are a table the consultant updates per tenant, and the model does not know which rule version applied on the treatment date. Institutions with 30,000 open trajectories cannot claim January, independent practitioners lose two months of cash flow, the March clarification means declarations already accepted must be corrected, and CRS's reputation for 'first time right' registration, its main argument against Nedap and SDB, becomes the reason a tender is lost.
stressors.businessReaction: Model the zorgprestatiemodel as a versioned financing rule set with effective dates, including settings, professions, consultation types, tariffs and mandatory referral rules; treat the referral as a first-class record with date, source and validity that intake, treatment plan and declaration share; add a registration completeness check that flags every open trajectory missing what next year's rule will require months before the deadline; recompute claims against the rule in force on the treatment date with a delta report when a rule is clarified retroactively; release tariff and rule updates centrally to all CRS tenants; align iJw and iWmo versions on the same mechanism; and turn the completeness check into a dashboard that the institution's registration team and HCI's consultants both use.
stressors.residue: Separate financing rule set version with effective date, setting and profession catalogue, tariff schedule, referral record with date, source and validity, registration completeness check and pre-submission gate, claim recomputation and retroactive delta, central tariff and rule release, and municipal message version. A claim knows which rule version, which referral and which check produced it, and an open trajectory knows what next year's rule will require of it.

impacts.effect: GGZ practitioners register once and the platform tells them months ahead what a coming rule change will need from each trajectory.
Institutions keep declarations compliant across insurers and municipalities because rules are versioned centrally, not configured per tenant.
The referral date is captured at intake as a record, so 'first time right' survives the 2026 rule.

stressors.name: Ransomware or a cloud outage takes the multi-tenant EPD down for thousands of practices in one NEN 7510 incident
stressors.detection: Alerts from the SOC on lateral movement or mass encryption in a shared environment, cloud provider status pages for the EU region that hosts the labels, failed backup verification or restore drills, NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 surveillance audit findings on segmentation and backup immutability, the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens 72-hour notification duty, Z-CERT advisories for the Dutch care sector, ransom notes in a consultant mailbox, dossier access from unusual locations in the audit log, support call volume during a login outage, therapists asking whether they may treat without seeing the dossier, insurers asking whether declarations were altered, practice owners tweeting screenshots of a blank agenda, and the number of tenants sharing one database or one identity provider.
stressors.attractor: On a Monday morning an attacker who entered through a compromised support account encrypts a shared database cluster, or the cloud region's storage service fails for eight hours. In the naive design thousands of practices share one environment, one identity provider and one backup schedule, consultants hold standing superuser rights, the dossier is unavailable when the database is, the agenda and online booking stop, declarations that were mid-submission are in an unknown state, and recovery is a runbook that has never been rehearsed at scale. 10,000 therapists cannot see who is in the waiting room or what was agreed last week, patients in Uw Zorg Online see error pages, HCI, as processor, must notify every affected practice, which as data controller has 72 hours to report to the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens, the WGBO and NEN 7510 obligations to keep the medical file available become the subject of a KNGF letter, and the 'one platform for all labels' promise of HCI One is read as 'one point of failure for all labels'.
stressors.businessReaction: Partition the runtime into cells with a bounded number of tenants, separate identity providers and immutable, tested backups per cell; make restore drills a scheduled practice with a measured recovery time per cell; give consultants time-bound, approved, logged access per tenant instead of standing rights; build a degraded mode in which today's agenda and a read-only dossier snapshot are served from a separate store; make declaration submission idempotent with a reconciled state per batch so an outage cannot lose or duplicate claims; compute the affected-tenant and affected-record set from the audit trail; map running controls continuously to NEN 7510 and ISO 27001 with evidence; prepare communication packs for practices, patients, the AP and Z-CERT; and publish availability and recovery targets per product.
stressors.residue: Separate tenant, cell and blast radius, identity provider per cell, immutable backup and restore drill with measured recovery time, break-glass access grant with justification and review, degraded mode with agenda and read-only dossier snapshot, idempotent submission batch with reconciled state, incident and affected-tenant and affected-record set, control evidence and certification scope, and communication pack. A dossier survives the database it lives in, and an incident has a computed scope rather than a guessed one.

impacts.effect: Practice owners can run today's agenda and read the dossier while the platform recovers, so a vendor incident is not a practice closure.

stressors.name: MedMij and Wegiz make PGO disclosure mandatory for paramedical care and every EPD must serve patients' data
stressors.detection: Wegiz general administrative orders (AMvB) designating a data exchange for paramedical or GGZ care, MedMij afsprakenstelsel releases and new information standards for physiotherapy or mental health, Nictiz publications and VWS roadmaps for the 'paramedische gegevensuitwisseling', VIPP-style subsidy schemes that pay providers for disclosure, KNGF and GGZ Nederland guidance on patient access, the number of MedMij-labelled PGOs (16 in November 2025) and their retrieval requests to HCI endpoints, patients asking their therapist why the physiotherapy dossier is not in their PGO, insurers writing disclosure into contracts, DVZA certification audits, questions from labels not yet on HCI One about how they will comply, and the share of practices that have consent and disclosure switched on.
stressors.attractor: VWS designates paramedical and mental health data exchange under Wegiz with a two-year deadline, MedMij publishes the information standard, and insurers add PGO disclosure to their 2027 contracts. In the naive design PGO disclosure is a Quli feature, each label has its own dossier model, consent is a checkbox in the intake, the DVZA endpoint exists for Uw Zorg Online's GP connections only, and paramedical dossiers hold free-text and label-specific fields that no information standard maps cleanly. Thousands of practices must disclose within a deadline, labels waiting for HCI One migration have no path, 16 PGOs start polling endpoints, patients see partial dossiers and complain, and HCI, which won a MedMij PGO tender and markets itself as the connected front door, is on the wrong side of the obligation for its own core customers.
stressors.businessReaction: Model disclosure as an obligation per care sector, information standard and version with an effective date; build one DVZA disclosure service that every label and HCI One feed from a canonical dossier mapping rather than per-label endpoints; treat patient consent and access as records shared across dossier, portal and PGO; make the information-standard mapping versioned and testable per discipline; expose disclosure coverage per practice and per data category as a dashboard; give labels that will not migrate before the deadline a read-only adapter into the shared service; keep MedMij certification scope and evidence as a property of the running service; and package disclosure as a subscription feature that insurers and subsidies can point to.
stressors.residue: Separate disclosure obligation per sector and information standard version, canonical dossier mapping per discipline, DVZA disclosure service shared across labels, patient consent and access record, PGO retrieval log, disclosure coverage per practice and data category, label adapter for non-migrated labels, and certification scope with evidence. A dossier is disclosable because it maps to a versioned standard, not because it lives in a particular label.

stressors.name: A label migration into HCI One stalls and practices churn to Intramed rather than wait
stressors.detection: Migration wave burn-down per label against the plan, data defect rate per migrated practice, parity gaps logged by consultants for features the old label had and HCI One does not, practices postponing their migration date more than twice, NPS and support ticket volume per label in the months after go-live, forum threads and KNGF regional meetings comparing HCI One with Intramed, Intramed's three-month free trial offers targeted at HCI labels, cancellation notices citing 'migration', renewal rates for labels announced as consolidating, churn of therapists who leave a practice and take the label choice to the next one, consultant utilisation on migration versus new sales, and the gap between Vortex's integration timeline and the actual per-discipline rollout.
stressors.attractor: The physiotherapy rollout of HCI One meets a wall: the SpotOnMedics group-management and BI features are not at parity, an Incura migration wave loses measurement history, and word spreads in the KNGF regions. In the naive design migration is a project per label with a date, data moves in one cut-over, a parity gap is a backlog item, and the old label is frozen the moment HCI One is announced. Practices that must choose between a frozen label and an unfinished platform pick the third option: Intramed, whose calculated 53 percent share of physiotherapy practices in the 2017 Marktdata survey, dated as it is, still marks it as the default alternative. A wave of 300 practices churns in six months, the frozen labels lose their best consultants to support the exodus, insurer contracts that reference the practice's software are re-papered, and 'no forced migration' becomes 'no migration at all' while the integration thesis behind the buyout is questioned at the board.
stressors.businessReaction: Model migration as waves per label and discipline with a parity gap register, a go/no-go gate per wave and a rehearsed rollback to the old label within a set window; keep every label on the shared declaration, disclosure and identity services so it stays current while it waits; migrate data through validated batches with a defect rate and reconciliation report per practice; measure practice sentiment and churn risk per label from support, usage and renewal signals and act on them before a wave; give practices a side-by-side period rather than a cut-over; make the old label's unique features explicit parity commitments with dates; and treat Intramed comparisons as a monitored competitive signal rather than anecdotes.
stressors.residue: Separate label and lifecycle state, migration wave with go/no-go gate, parity gap register with commitment, migration batch with defect rate and reconciliation, rollback window, side-by-side period, shared service membership per label, practice sentiment and churn risk signal, and competitive signal. A practice can move to HCI One, stay on its label or move back without losing data or declarations.

stressors.name: Insurers move paramedical contracting to outcomes and pay on PROMs and LDF data instead of treatments
stressors.detection: Zorgverzekeraars Nederland and individual insurer purchasing policies for physiotherapy that add outcome and PROM conditions, contract tiers ('plus' contracts) that require Keurmerk registration, LDF participation and minimum PROM completion, NZa experiments with bundled or outcome-based paramedical payment, KNGF and Keurmerk Fysiotherapie benchmark releases, the share of practices whose contract references LDF or PROM completion, PROM completion rates per practice against the insurer threshold, opt-in consent rates for LDF delivery, insurer requests for practice-level outcome extracts, practice owners asking how their benchmark compares before contract season, and revenue at risk per practice from missed thresholds.
stressors.attractor: The largest insurers move physiotherapy to contracts where a share of the tariff depends on PROM completion, outcome benchmarks from the LDF and Keurmerk audits, and a bundled payment for common complaints replaces per-treatment claims. In the naive design PROMs are optional instruments a therapist may add, LDF delivery is a monthly export the practice can switch off, the benchmark comes back from the LDF months later, the contract is a tariff table, and the declaration engine only knows treatments. Practices discover in November that they missed a completion threshold worth eight percent of revenue, the benchmark shows them below average with no explanation, and the practices on labels without integrated PROMs look for a system that 'does outcomes', which competitors and exercise partners advertise loudly.
stressors.businessReaction: Model the contract as a type with outcome measures, thresholds and payment rules per insurer; make PROM collection a scheduled part of every care pathway with completion tracked per trajectory and consent per patient; deliver LDF and Keurmerk data as a governed data product with a practice-level mirror so the practice sees its own outcomes before the insurer does; add bundled and outcome-based payment forms to the declaration engine next to treatment claims; show revenue at risk per contract condition in the practice dashboard during the year, not after; let patients complete PROMs from the app and see their own progress; and offer benchmark and contract-readiness reports as a service to practices and to insurers.
stressors.residue: Separate contract type with outcome measure, threshold and payment rule, PROM schedule per care pathway, completion and consent per trajectory, payer data product with practice-level mirror, benchmark with explanation, bundled and outcome-based payment form, and revenue-at-risk per contract condition. A treatment knows which contract condition it contributes to, and a practice sees its outcome position before contract season.

impacts.effect: Practice owners see their outcome and contract position all year and are paid on results without extra administration.
Allied health disciplines show outcomes to payers with the same PROM and benchmark machinery.
Patients complete PROMs from the app and see their own progress.
PROMs are scheduled by the care pathway so quality data comes from treatment, not extra typing.
Bundled and outcome-based payments are declared and reconciled next to treatment claims.
Progress and outcomes are reported to patients and payers from the same measurement series.

stressors.name: An AI voice-to-text error in a clinical note reaches a treatment decision and a complaint
stressors.detection: A tuchtcollege or complaints committee case that cites a dictated note, a therapist reporting that the transcript inverted 'left' and 'right' or a medication dose, the share of AI-generated notes signed without edit, edit distance between transcript and signed note per therapist, model and provider version changes announced by the speech vendor, the EU AI Act classification of clinical documentation tools and the Inspectie Gezondheidszorg en Jeugd's stance, professional bodies (KNGF, NIP, NVvP) issuing guidance on AI documentation, patients asking under the WGBO who wrote their record, insurer audits questioning summaries, data-processing questions about audio leaving the EU, and practices switching the feature off after a scare.
stressors.attractor: A GGZ practitioner dictates a session summary, SmartAI transcribes a suicide-risk statement as its negation, the note is signed unedited, a colleague acts on it, and the case ends at the tuchtcollege with the note as evidence. In the naive design the transcript replaces the therapist's text, the model version and provider are invisible, there is no record of what was edited, audio is sent to whichever provider was cheapest, the feature is on for everyone with no per-tenant policy, and HCI cannot say which model produced which sentence. The IGJ asks HCI for its risk classification, institutions demand the feature be disabled, KNGF advises members to review every AI note, the productivity story behind HCI One's 'more time for care' collapses, and a competitor launches 'AI you can audit'.
stressors.businessReaction: Model AI documentation as a capability with provider, model version, region and a per-tenant policy; keep transcript provenance so every sentence in a note knows whether it came from a model, a template or a person and what was edited; require clinical sign-off with a visible diff and flag risk-bearing phrases (laterality, dosage, risk statements) for confirmation; keep audio and transcripts under the same data class and retention as the dossier; monitor unedited-sign-off rates and transcript error rates per model version and tenant; classify the capability under the AI Act with evidence; give practices and institutions the switch, the policy and the audit report; and publish the human-review guarantee as part of the proposition.
stressors.residue: Separate AI capability with provider, model version and region, per-tenant AI policy, transcript provenance per sentence, human edit record and sign-off with diff, risk-phrase confirmation, audio and transcript data class and retention, error and unedited-sign-off metrics, and AI Act classification evidence. A note knows which model, which edit and which person produced each part, and a practice can turn the model off without losing the note.

stressors.name: A GP information system vendor launches its own patient app and drops the Uw Zorg Online connection
stressors.detection: Announcements by Pharmapartners, CGM, Sanday or HealthConnected of a bundled patient app or portal, HIS contract renewals that make the vendor's own app the default, deprecation notices for the HIS connector API used by Uw Zorg Online, MedMij connections from HIS vendors' own DVZA endpoints, the share of Uw Zorg Online's 4 million users whose GP runs each HIS, GP practice managers asking whether they need two apps, patients receiving a second invitation from the HIS app, e-consult and repeat-prescription volumes per HIS falling, LHV and pharmacy association guidance on portal choice, connector error rates after HIS releases, and the number of practices whose Uw Zorg Online contract is bundled with the HIS.
stressors.attractor: One of the GP and pharmacy system vendors to which Uw Zorg Online connects (Pharmapartners, CGM, Sanday, HealthConnected, Bricks or Vertimart) launches its own patient app, bundles it into the HIS licence, and gives twelve months' notice on the connector Uw Zorg Online uses for agenda, e-consult and repeat prescriptions. In the naive design the patient relationship belongs to the connector: without the HIS connection the GP disappears from the app, the patient's history of messages and prescriptions is stranded, and the practice website's e-consult button points nowhere. A million patients receive a 'download our new app' letter from their GP, HCI's consumer front door loses a quarter of its active users in a year, pharmacies connected through the same HIS follow, Quli's MedMij retrieval keeps working but nobody uses a PGO for an e-consult, and the network-platform story that justifies the Uw Zorg Online merger loses its largest channel.
stressors.businessReaction: Model the patient's relationship with a practice as HCI's own record, independent of any HIS connector, with the connector as one channel among several; support multiple channels per practice (HIS connector, MedMij, direct EPD for paramedical and GGZ, e-mail and secure messaging fallback) with a fallback path when a connector is deprecated; keep the patient's message and prescription history in the app under the patient's consent regardless of which connector produced it; make HIS connectors versioned adapters with monitored deprecation windows and migration plans; deepen the channels HIS vendors cannot replace, such as cross-provider triage, network care and paramedical and GGZ access in one app; offer GP practices a portal that works across HIS choices as a reason to keep it; and track channel concentration per HIS as a business risk.
stressors.residue: Separate patient-practice relationship record, patient channel and connector, channel fallback route, connector adapter version with deprecation window and migration plan, message and prescription history under patient consent, cross-provider service (triage, network care), and channel concentration metric. A patient's relationship with a practice survives the connector that once carried it.

stressors.name: GGZ institutions consolidate onto SDB and Nedap and CRS is locked out of the top 50
stressors.detection: The annual M&I/Partners inventory of EPD and portal choices among the 50 largest GGZ organisations (SDB Groep 30 percent, Nedap 27 percent in 2025), tender notices on TenderNed for GGZ EPD replacements, mergers between GGZ institutions and the EPD chosen by the surviving entity, GGZ Friesland-style switches announced in the trade press, portal share of Caren and Karify against Quli, CRS renewal conversations that mention 'landscape harmonisation', institutions asking for VVT and disability modules that CRS does not offer, integration partners (Minddistrict, Therapieland) prioritising the larger EPDs, CRS's share of new independent-practitioner sign-ups, and the number of CRS institutions above 500 professionals.
stressors.attractor: Two mid-sized CRS institutions merge with larger organisations on SDB USER and Nedap Ons, a third loses a tender to PinkRoccade on portal and integration criteria, and the next M&I inventory shows no CRS institution among the top 50. In the naive design CRS is one product for institutions, practices and youth care, the client portal competes with Caren and Karify on features alone, tenders are answered from scratch, an exiting institution's data leaves through a bespoke export, and the GGZ business unit's revenue depends on a handful of large contracts. Integration partners deprioritise CRS, Embloom's institutional pipeline follows the EPD choice, the unit's economics tilt to many small practices with lower prices, and the roll-up's GGZ leg looks like a portfolio that should be sold rather than grown.
stressors.businessReaction: Model the GGZ market as segments (large institutions, mid-sized organisations, independent practices, youth care) with a proposition, tender package and pricing per segment; make CRS plus Embloom plus Quli one integrated proposition with portal parity against Caren and Karify measured per feature; treat tenders as a reusable package with reference architectures, integration catalogue and certification evidence; make the client portal and e-health usable with other EPDs so Embloom and Quli win even where CRS loses; provide a clean exit and data-portability path so an institution that leaves speaks well of HCI and can come back; and focus CRS growth where the top 50 vendors are weak: independent practices, youth care and multi-financier registration.
stressors.residue: Separate institution segment and proposition, tender package with reference architecture and evidence, portal parity register, integrated GGZ proposition (CRS, Embloom, Quli), EPD-independent e-health and portal, exit and data-portability path, and segment revenue concentration metric. Losing an EPD tender does not lose the e-health, the portal or the relationship.

stressors.name: Labour shortage and 'ontregel de zorg' change what practices are willing to pay for
stressors.detection: VWS 'Ontregel de zorg' programme reports and the Integraal Zorgakkoord commitments to cut administrative burden, KNGF and VFW surveys on the working day per week lost to administration and the one in five therapists reporting stress-related disability, Nivel counts of physiotherapists and practices, vacancy rates and waiting lists in GGZ exceeding the Treeknorm in every region, practices asking for 'fewer clicks' rather than more modules in renewal talks, usage data showing which modules go untouched, competitors pricing on automation rather than per user, insurer pressure to reduce administrative conditions, therapists leaving practices for employment in hospitals or leaving the profession, and the share of practices willing to pay for billing services, AI documentation and automated reminders versus base licences.
stressors.attractor: Practices lose therapists faster than they can hire, insurers and VWS strip administrative conditions in the 'ontregel' programme, and the value practices will pay for shifts from an EPD that stores administration to a service that removes it. In the naive design HCI prices per user per label, value is the module list, automation is a feature inside a module, and the billing service, AI documentation and reminders are add-ons sold by consultants. Practices with fewer therapists pay less per user while asking for more automation, compare HCI One with per-practice flat offers, and a competitor bundles 'we handle your declarations and your notes' as the price. The residues already carried, versioned declaration rules, referral and completeness checks, cells and degraded mode, are tested by whether they can be packaged and metered as administrative relief rather than as software.
stressors.businessReaction: Measure administrative burden per practice as a product metric (minutes per treatment, clicks per declaration, unedited AI notes, rejections corrected without practice involvement) and report it to the practice; package automation as entitlements (automated declaration correction, PROM scheduling, reminders, AI documentation, billing service) with value-based pricing per practice rather than per user; reuse the declaration rule sets and completeness checks so automation is a policy switch, not a project; position HCI One and CRS as the answer to labour shortage with the burden metric as proof; and align sales, support and product on the same metric so a renewal conversation starts from minutes saved.
stressors.residue: Separate administrative-burden metric per practice, automation entitlement, value-based package and price per practice, automation policy switch on existing rule sets and checks, and relief evidence in renewal. The loop test: the platform survives the shift when the residues from the declaration, financing and continuity stressors can be metered and sold as relief without new structure.
